consistency.verdict:
The doc mostly reflects both rulings. The names memory_digest, memory_digest_generated, submit_memory_digest, MemoryDigestClient and settle_pending_memory_digests are used consistently, and day_digest, 零点回顾, 核验摘要 and 格子 no longer appear. Budget sums hold (100+3,000+2,400+6,000=11,500; 800+700+1,000+500=3,000), as do the example sizes (6,388 total, longest digest 144 chars) and the pilot total of about $18.

The remaining problems:
- One pre-ruling leftover contradicts ruling (1): the F14 row says months and years use deterministic statistics.
- The rule-text phase table never moves rules[0] or rules[2] to the final text. P2 would ship a rules[2] that points at 人设层 noted_on after P2 has removed preferences from 人设层.
- Several P1 and P2 features depend on search_memory, which ships only in P3: folding and its retrieval line, overflow of 长期, and days 4+.

- 第五章 calls items 8 and 9 settled but each still has an open sub-question. Item 23 still offers an option that ruling (1) rules out.
- Absolute statements contradict the doc's own fallbacks: past days appear only as paragraphs (but missing digests fall back to raw entries), and the month digest never reads events (but it gets event-derived counts).
- The 12-item search cap contradicts the claim that a range query returns about 16 or 5 days.
- The example digests use Chinese numerals, which the doc's own prompt forbids.
- The 05-recording-engine.md section is deleted while the code keeps reflection checks for historical runs.
- Several minor number, citation and naming slips.

rulings.verdict: The final (P3) design mostly follows both rulings. The day, month and year tiers are LLM-written paragraphs, and the 长期 view list (裁决 17) and the raw-entry fallback (裁决 23) are flagged. search_memory is the only memory tool in P3, recall_task_summary stays as it is, and no AS2 built-in tool or MEMORY.md reaches any prompt (V event 6015 has exactly 10 tools and its prompt contains no MEMORY.md content). Two gaps in rulings coverage remain. First, the doc says each phase can ship on its own, yet it keeps the three memory_* tools, which return raw episode rows, open to the LLM through P1 and P2 without flagging this. Second, plan_day keeps reading yesterday as concatenated event rows, while the doc says events are no longer shown to the model as memory. Four of the nine 近三天 example paragraphs contain invented details. Every one of them still passes the doc's own number and name guards. The examples also break the prompt's Arabic-numeral rule, and the one wrong number among them is written in Chinese numerals.

issues.problem: Ruling (2) says search_memory is the only memory tool and the three memory_* tools are deleted. The doc deletes them only in P3, and it says every phase can ship on its own (「每一期都可以单独上线」, :625). So in a shipped P1 or P2 the LLM keeps memory_recent, memory_search and memory_time_range with their descriptions. The unchanged rule 「提交前可以查询记忆或回看任务」 still teaches it to use them. These tools return raw episodes.jsonl rows from any past day, so they also reintroduce concatenated past-day rows that ruling (1) excludes. The read-only path also keeps the memory tools until P3. This interim deviation is never flagged as a decision: the P1/P2 rule table (:410-414) only says the earlier versions 「不提 memory_*」 and does not remove the tools.

risk.verdict: The doc reflects both rulings correctly. Compaction is model-written at the day, month and year tiers. search_memory is the only memory tool, recall_task_summary is kept, and the tool count goes from 10 to 8. Several things hold up: the digest never mutates state, and the groceries gate is enforced by the environment (location_activities.py:62-87), so a wrong memory cannot make cooking possible without a kit. LabelKit cuts unknown kinds down to {kind} (export_source.py:355-357). The export timeline reads only activity_progress and action_result (timeline_labels.py:68-75). Transport failures mirror plan_day's failure evidence (day_planning.py:195-203). Replay reads events, and after the checkpoint it regenerates digests exactly as plan_day does. Multi-agent midnight latency does not apply, because the world requires exactly one agent (world.py:109-111). The plan_day analogue in V took 1.9–4.1 s per attempt, with retries on 3 of 5 days, so the digest adds only seconds per midnight. The real gaps sit where ruling (1) makes model paragraphs the only past memory. (a) The invented home dinners come from a catalog summary shown in the start and completion results, which the kit sentence does not touch, and the 'tightened' food guard does not catch the doc's own example. (b) The guards check only that a name or number appears somewhere in the input, not what it is paired with, so swapped kits and wrong meal slots pass. (c) A failed digest renders as the same null as 'no records'. (d) No pilot metric or acceptance criterion measures whether a digest is faithful or complete. Month and year drift, source_event_ids provenance, and the memory gates are minor gaps.

issues.problem: The doc understates what the guards miss. They check only that each name and each digit string appears somewhere in the category's input, never what it is paired with. Swapping the kit that was cooked with the one just ordered passes every guard. So do calling breakfast lunch and moving one item's time or price onto another. Digits such as 10, 9 and 12 occur in every 核验 line through dates and times. This is exactly the error the V persona made (10-11: it believed the 板栗烧鸡 kit was still for dinner after using it at lunch), and after midnight the digest is all the model sees. Line 114 「名称和数字守卫拦住编造」, line 754 「数字守卫能拦住编造」 (the basis for recommending option A in 裁决 8) and rules[1] 「回顾里的名称、时刻和价钱都出自当时的记录」 all overstate the protection.

The persona cannot tell 'nothing happened in this category that day' from 'that day's memory was not compacted'. Since past days exist only as digests, a null food cell reads as having eaten nothing. issues.quote: 每天调用次数、重试、fallback、三道守卫各自的丢弃次数、回顾被引用的比例
issues.problem: No pilot metric or P1 acceptance criterion measures whether a digest is correct or complete. The metrics measure only whether a digest exists (M3), whether it is cited (M1, M10) and how often guards fire (M10). M1 counts a citation of a wrongly written dish as success. The verification table is left 「供人工抽查」 with no sample size, no pass criterion and no named reviewer. 裁决 23 admits omissions become invisible to the model after midnight, but the omission rate is never measured. P1 can therefore pass while digests drop lunches or swap kits, and M4 (lunch repetition) cannot be traced back to memory quality.

issues.quote: 每一级只压缩下一级：月回顾读那个月的日回顾，年回顾读那一年的月回顾，都不回头读事件
issues.problem: This contradicts :275 and :319, where the month digest also gets per-category counts that code computes from committed events. The year digest gets no such counts, so year-level text can only be checked against month-level text, and an error in a day digest has no factual anchor by the time it reaches the year. At month level the number guard only checks that a digit string occurs, so 「番茄牛肉刀削面 5 次」 passes whenever a 5 appears anywhere in the input; the count line does not constrain anything. Not letting the day digest read earlier digests does not stop errors carrying forward either: the persona writes each day's self-reports while looking at the 近三天 digests and the 「长期」 views, and those self-reports feed the next day's digest. In V, 「番茄炒蛋配清炒青菜」 was carried from 10-08 through 10-12.
issues.evidence: Doc :252 vs :275 「另附代码算出的每类次数统计作背景」 and :319 (the counts are pure functions of committed events). Doc :275-276 gives the year tier only month digests. Doc :115 justifies not reading earlier digests with 「接上会把旧印象续写进新的一天」. V: requests carrying the phrase are 21 on 10-08, 86 on 10-09, 89 on 10-10, 69 on 10-11 and 90 on 10-12.
issues.fix: 改为：「每一级只压缩下一级的文字；月回顾和年回顾另附代码从事件算出的每类次数统计（年回顾按年统计）。月、年回顾里写次数时，必须照抄统计行（如「番茄牛肉刀削面 3 次」）作为连续子串，否则按数字守卫不通过重试。」P3 验收加「跨月试点里月回顾写到的次数与统计逐条相符」。

issues.quote: 日回顾的 `source_event_ids` 是它所引条目背后的事件
issues.problem: refs need only be non-empty (:281), so a digest narrating the whole day can cite just n1. Deriving `source_event_ids` from refs then understates provenance. This is the digest event's only provenance field, and compare_runs maps it by event identity, so audits and causal tracing read an incomplete source set while it looks authoritative.
issues.evidence: Doc :281 「refs 非空，且都属于这一类的编号」. Doc :322 builds source_event_ids from the cited entries. The Chapter 3 code table adds the path data.digests.*.source_event_ids[] to compare_runs.py.
